subject: Behavioral Economics
title: The Focal Point Bias
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Focal Point Bias.

hook.text: Asked to meet a stranger in New York with no plan, most people choose Grand Central at noon.

buildup.text: Schelling found that people converge on obvious, prominent points when coordination is needed.

discovery.text: Focal points: when uncertain, we gravitate toward whatever stands out or feels like the default answer.

twist.text: In negotiation, round numbers become focal points. A $100k salary feels natural; $97k feels strange.

climax.text: Focal points simplify coordination. But they also limit creativity by making the obvious feel mandatory.

punchline.text: The obvious choice is often just the laziest one.

quiz.question: What are Schelling focal points?
options: The most expensive options in a negotiation
Obvious choices people converge on without communication

details.summary: Focal point bias causes people to give disproportionate weight to the most prominent or salient feature of a situation. The focal point captures attention and dominates the judgment, while equally or more important but less salient features are underweighted or ignored.
details.whyItMatters: Focal point bias explains why people fixate on price when quality matters more, on headline numbers when context is essential, and on the most visible metric when hidden factors drive outcomes. Attention drives judgment more than relevance does.
takeaways: The most salient feature of a decision dominates judgment disproportionately
Less visible but equally important factors are systematically underweighted
What captures attention first becomes the focal anchor for all subsequent reasoning

faq.question: How does focal point bias differ from anchoring?
faq.answer: Anchoring involves a specific number that distorts estimates. Focal point bias is broader: any salient feature, whether numerical, visual, or conceptual, captures disproportionate weight in judgment. A bright color, a dramatic story, or a headline metric can all become focal points.

faq.question: How can you counteract focal point bias in analysis?
faq.answer: Create structured evaluation frameworks that force consideration of all relevant factors with pre-assigned weights. This prevents the most salient factor from dominating. Ask what you might be underweighting because it is less visible or dramatic.
